newsitem.title: UK: UK army vows to crack down on troublesome troops.
newsitem.headline: UK army vows to crack down on troublesome troops.

text.p: The British army, reacting to a rash of violent incidents involving its troops, on Tuesday vowed to crack down on offenders but denied that overall discipline levels were falling.
This month alone five British soldiers have been accused of attacking holidaymakers in Cyprus while drunken off-duty troops smashed up hotel rooms in the Uruguayan capital Montevideo.

"It doesn't matter at all where or when these incidents occur. We in the army find them totally unacceptable. We totally condemn this sort of behaviour," Major-General Mike Wilcox, assistant chief of the general staff, told BBC radio.
"The army takes any allegation or any incident extremely seriously. We always investigate them thoroughly and then we severely punish the culprits when they're proven guilty."

The latest attack in Cyprus prompted the British base authorities to impose a ban on visits to Ayia Napa by members of the Kings regiment, just one month after another ban on soldiers' visits to the area was lifted.

The restrictions were first imposed in September 1994 after the killing of a Danish tour guide by three members of the Royal Greenjackets regiment. They are now serving a life sentence in Cyprus's central prison.

"Nothing's wrong with the army. These are isolated incidents, they're not symptomatic of wider disciplinary problems... You will always get one or two isolated incidents by individuals, usually where alcohol is concerned," Wilcox said.

"The sadness is that we've got some 170,000 people including the Territorial Army (auxiliary troops) doing a wonderful job worldwide in Bosnia and Northern Ireland and the isolated stupidity and behaviour of a few just tarnish our image."
